meta.disclaimer: Not legal advice. This is a plain-English summary of public sources, kept for marketing planning, and rules change. Check with your state bar and your own counsel before you run an ad.
meta.notice: Probative is a marketing firm, not a law firm; not legal advice.

summary: The lawyer advertising rules of every US state and DC, in plain English: ad filing, what each ad must include, waiting periods for injury contact, claims and testimonials, referral and lead rules, ads in other languages, call-recording consent, texting law and privacy law, plus state laws on drug and medical-device ads. Each cell cites its official source with the words quoted, and says how it was checked (P, D or U).

P.label: Primary source
P.meaning: We read the rule, statute, court order, bar page or regulator page itself.

S.label: Secondary source
S.meaning: A summary or quotation of the rule by a legal-marketing firm, law firm or tracker. We check it against the official text before relying on it for a client.

D.label: ABA model default
D.meaning: The state’s own text isn’t read at an official source yet, so the ABA Model Rule or our national default applies until it is. The cell says why.

U.label: Open question
U.meaning: Unknown or unsettled; a lawyer must answer it.

topics.label: Waiting period for targeted injury contact
Ads in Spanish and other languages

federal.text: No unsolicited contact about injury claims within 45 days after an air-carrier or passenger-rail accident, in every state.
Marketing calls and texts placed by autodialer, or with a prerecorded or artificial voice (AI voices included), need prior express written consent; opt-outs are honored within 10 business days.

sources.label: FCC on AI-generated voices in robocalls

federal.text: The FTC rule on consumer reviews and testimonials (16 CFR Part 465, in force since October 21, 2024) bans fake, bought and AI-generated reviews, undisclosed insider reviews and review suppression.

sources.label: FTC, Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule: questions and answers

federal.text: Google bars remarketing, Customer Match and lookalike audiences in sensitive categories such as health and trauma. Conversion uploads for bidding remain allowed.

Local Services Ads screen each lawyer’s bar license, and advertisers can’t sell or pass leads to other businesses. Since October 1, 2026, a business-hours missed call is billed as a lead when the caller stays on more than 20 seconds.

federal.text: Since September 2026, Google no longer offers campaign language targeting on Search and Performance Max; ads serve by matching the language of the search to the language of the ad.

federal.text: Every bar opinion we found says the same thing: don't reveal client information to answer a bad online review. A short, general reply or none at all is the safe course (ABA Formal Op. 496, 2021, plus NY, TX, FL, CO, AZ, OR and WI opinions in the ethics-opinions dataset).

federal.text: Bars that address it treat a website or intake chatbot as the firm's own communication: it must not mislead or give legal advice, Florida says it must identify itself as AI, and a lawyer must supervise it (Florida Op. 24-1, Oregon Op. 2026-208, Alabama Op. 2026-01 and WSBA AO 202505). No bar opinion we found is mainly about AI-made images or voices in ads.

sources.quote: careful when using generative AI chatbot for advertising and intake purposes as the lawyer will be ultimately responsible

abaDefaults.text: Where a cell is marked D, the ABA Model Rule default applies until the state’s own text is checked.
points: Results only if truthful and given in context.
“Certified specialist” only through an approved body that the ad names.
Lawyers may pay reasonable advertising costs and a qualified referral service’s usual charges, but never for a recommendation.
Lead generators are allowed only if they don’t recommend the lawyer, imply a recommendation or split fees.
Every ad names at least one responsible lawyer or firm, with contact information (Rule 7.2(d)).

sources.label: ABA Model Rule 7.2 and its comments
ABA Model Rule 7.3 and its comments

ourDefaults: The responsible lawyer’s name and office city in every ad, in pinned text, the image or the video.
No targeted contact with injured people, and no geofencing of hospitals, clinics, accident scenes, police stations or courthouses.
No dollar results, testimonials, awards, “best”, “expert” or “specialist” in ads unless the state’s rules clear the exact wording.
We never refer, recommend or route people to lawyers, never sell leads and never price per lead or per case.
Every required statement appears in each language the ad uses.
A recording notice opens every tracked call, in every state.
Callbacks 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. in the caller’s time zone, at most 3 attempts in 24 hours, with no autodialers, prerecorded or AI voices.
Forms ask only what intake needs; tags fire only after consent; injury details never reach ad platforms.
Location targeting by presence only, with every targeted state’s rules loaded into the ad check.

statutes.quote: A person or entity may, if otherwise permitted by the laws or rules of court of a State, bring in an appropriate court of that State
statutes.text: Anyone who receives a call or text that breaks the TCPA's autodialer or prerecorded-voice rules may sue for an injunction and the greater of actual loss or $500 per violation, up to three times that if willful or knowing.
statutes.textEs: Quien reciba una llamada o un mensaje que infrinja las reglas de la TCPA sobre marcadores automáticos o voces grabadas puede demandar para que se detenga y por la cantidad mayor entre la pérdida real o 500 dólares por infracción, hasta el triple si fue intencional o a sabiendas.

statutes.quote: Before the hour of 8 a.m. or after 9 p.m. (local time at the called party's location)
statutes.text: Telephone solicitations to a residence are barred before 8 a.m. and after 9 p.m., local time where the called person is, in every state.
statutes.textEs: Las llamadas de venta a una residencia están prohibidas antes de las 8 a. m. y después de las 9 p. m., hora local del lugar de la persona llamada, en todos los estados.

statutes.quote: where such person is a party to the communication or where one of the parties to the communication has given prior consent to such interception
statutes.text: Federal law lets a party to a call, or someone with one party's prior consent, record it, unless the purpose is a crime or a tort. State law can be stricter.
statutes.textEs: La ley federal permite grabar una llamada a quien participa en ella o a quien tiene el consentimiento previo de una de las partes, salvo que el fin sea un delito o un ilícito civil. La ley estatal puede ser más estricta.

statutes.cite: Insurance Marketing Coalition v. FCC, No. 24-10277 (11th Cir. Jan. 24, 2025)
statutes.quote: we grant IMC's petition for review, vacate Part III.D of the 2023 Order, and remand for further proceedings
statutes.text: The Eleventh Circuit vacated the FCC's 2023 one-to-one consent rule for robocalls and robotexts, so prior express consent is read as the statute words it.
statutes.textEs: El Tribunal de Apelaciones del Undécimo Circuito anuló la regla de la FCC de 2023 sobre el consentimiento individual para llamadas y mensajes automatizados, por lo que el consentimiento previo y expreso se interpreta según el texto de la ley.

tcpaConsent.topic: Consent before calling or texting a web-form lead
tcpaConsent.text: A telemarketing or advertising call to a cell number that uses an autodialer or an artificial or prerecorded voice needs the called party's prior express written consent under 47 CFR 64.1200(a)(2), and the FCC has ruled that AI-generated human voices count as an artificial or prerecorded voice. Prior express written consent is a signed written agreement that names the phone number, with a clear and conspicuous disclosure that signing authorizes autodialed or prerecorded telemarketing and that signing is not required as a condition of purchase; an electronic signature counts if it is valid under federal or state law (47 CFR 64.1200(f)(9)). The person can revoke consent by any reasonable method, including replying "stop" to a text, and the request must be honored within a reasonable time not to exceed ten business days (47 CFR 64.1200(a)(10)). The FCC's one-to-one consent rule, which would have limited each consent to one seller, was vacated by the Eleventh Circuit on Jan. 24, 2025.
tcpaConsent.textEs: Una llamada de telemercadeo o publicidad a un numero celular que usa un marcador automatico o una voz artificial o pregrabada requiere el consentimiento expreso por escrito previo de la persona que recibe la llamada, segun 47 CFR 64.1200(a)(2); la FCC resolvio que las voces humanas generadas con IA cuentan como voz artificial o pregrabada. El consentimiento expreso por escrito es un acuerdo escrito y firmado que indica el numero de telefono, con una revelacion clara y destacada de que la firma autoriza el telemercadeo con marcador automatico o voz pregrabada y de que firmar no es obligatorio como condicion de compra; una firma electronica cuenta si es valida segun la ley federal o estatal (47 CFR 64.1200(f)(9)). La persona puede revocar el consentimiento por cualquier metodo razonable, incluso respondiendo "stop" a un mensaje de texto, y la solicitud debe atenderse en un plazo razonable que no exceda diez dias habiles (47 CFR 64.1200(a)(10)). La regla de la FCC de consentimiento uno a uno, que habria limitado cada consentimiento a un solo vendedor, fue anulada por el Undecimo Circuito el 24 de enero de 2025.
tcpaConsent.note: The eCFR page for 47 CFR 64.1200 carries a banner 'cross reference link to an amendment published at 91 FR 67219, Oct. 26, 2026'; that amendment's content was not read, so the quoted paragraphs are the current eCFR text as retrieved 2026-10-28 and could be changed by it. The rule text says 'artificial or prerecorded voice'; the AI-voice point rests on the FCC declaratory ruling FCC 24-17 (Feb. 2024). Whether a given lead-form follow-up is 'telemarketing' or 'advertising' (versus informational) is a fact question the rule text does not answer. The (a)(2) paragraph reaches the lines in (a)(1)(i)-(iii), which include cellular numbers.
